video_title: Boogie & Lou on Jayson Tatum & Jaylen Brown BEEF + Lou Predicts Jaylen Brown for DPOY!

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams and Chandler Parsons on Jayson Tatum vs. Scottie Pippen comparison
quotes.excerpt: If he is more Pippen than Kobe, he's still in the same conversation and the same tier of players.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I'm not buying it because that is said in a way that Pippen is less than something. Scottie Pippen is a top 50 player of all time. If he is more Pippen than Kobe, he's still in the same conversation and the same tier of players. Obviously Kobe Bryant is Kobe Bryant, but we're not going to dress this thing up as any type of disrespect toward Scottie Pippen at all. If Colin Cowherd is trying to say there are some tier A1 guys and some tier AB guys, I'm going to leave that up to Colin Cowherd to defend on his own. But if Jayson Tatum is more Scottie Pippen than Kobe Bryant, then give me both.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: I'm not buying that either. One, I think Jayson Tatum is Jayson Tatum. He's an incredible player, he's a great player in this league, he's earned everything that comes his way. Scottie Pippen has done that and so has Kobe Bryant. I don't understand the comparison. I feel like he's trying to say he's not the main guy.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown's team dynamic
quotes.excerpt: Those two guys are both champions, they're both superstars in this league and they've both shown that they're proven winners.
quotes.quote: Those two guys are both champions, they're both superstars in this league and they've both shown that they're proven winners. So all the other extra stuff, I'm more concerned about figuring out their dynamic and what the real thing was. I care more about that than trying to sit here and diminish them as players or as individuals as teammates. Jayson Tatum is Jayson Tatum. He's great, he's still going to continue to be great, he's a champion, he's been a winner since he stepped foot in.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams and Chandler Parsons on Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown's competitive relationship
quotes.excerpt: There isn't probably a personal problem where they have a certain disdain for each other, but competitively, Jaylen Brown told him, stay ready at all times, dog.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: There isn't probably a personal problem where they have a certain disdain for each other, but competitively, Jaylen Brown told him, stay ready at all times, dog. It ain't sweet. I love the fact that we're keeping this in perspective. We're not going to allow the media to run off with certain narratives like they still will. But hey, listen, there's not a personal problem, but every time I run into you on this basketball court, it's all the way up to the rafters. It's up.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Beef where I'm from, I don't believe it is. Do I think it's animosity? Do I think it's some type of competitive nature brewing between the two? Absolutely, I think it's always been there. I think that's also why those two are as good as they are. Iron sharpens iron. If I'm battling against a guy like that every single day in practice, after practice, individuals, one-on-ones, I'm going to get better.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on Jaylen Brown as the best two-way player
quotes.excerpt: I'm buying that he's definitely the best two-way player in the league.
quotes.quote: I'm buying that he's definitely the best two-way player in the league. Usually we give that type of title to the guys that play the two or they play the three and Jaylen Brown has been exceptional on both ends of the floor, especially what he was able to do last year and how he's able to fit into what Philly is building right now. If Victor Wembanyama didn't exist in this league, we would probably be having a different conversation around Jaylen Brown's name on the defensive end because offensively we know what he's able to do. He's carried teams to the promised land with his offensive abilities and he's been able to be dynamic on the defensive end with his defensive abilities. I'm going to go out on a limb and say he might be defensive player of the year this season, why not?
